headline: 4 issues found, 3 serious. Fix the serious ones before ordering boards.

findings.what: Two separate connections, "+5V" and "GND", are touching, near x=112.0 mm, y=100.0 mm on the back copper layer (B.Cu).
findings.why: These are meant to be electrically separate. Where they touch they become one connection (a short), so "+5V" and "GND" will be forced to the same voltage. That usually means the board does the wrong thing, and if one is a power rail it can pull large current and overheat.
findings.fix: separate the two nets' copper: widen the gap or reroute so the trace/pad spacing clears the clearance rule

findings.what: Two separate connections, "+5V" and "GND", are touching, near x=112.0 mm, y=100.0 mm on the front copper layer (F.Cu).
findings.why: These are meant to be electrically separate. Where they touch they become one connection (a short), so "+5V" and "GND" will be forced to the same voltage. That usually means the board does the wrong thing, and if one is a power rail it can pull large current and overheat.
findings.fix: separate the two nets' copper: widen the gap or reroute so the trace/pad spacing clears the clearance rule

findings.what: A gate or select input on Q1 has no pull resistor. net 'GATE_CTRL' drives 1 MOSFET gate (Q1) and is held only by U1 pin 14 with no pull-up or pull-down resistor. While the MCU is in reset or booting (or the cable is unplugged) the pin is high-impedance, so the node floats and the transistor may conduct or sit half-on. Add a pull resistor (about 100 kilohms) to the level that is safe at power-up.
findings.why: A microcontroller pin is high-impedance while it resets and boots, and a connector pin is open when the cable is out. An input driven only from such a pin has no level then, so a transistor can turn on or a switch can pick the wrong side for as long as the pin is undefined.
findings.fix: Add a pull-down or pull-up resistor (about 100 kilohms) to the level that is safe when the part is off.

findings.what: the board is not routed yet, so it cannot be ordered as is: no copper joins its 6 pad group(s)
findings.why: No track, via or copper pour joins any of the placed pads yet, so a board made from these files would connect nothing. The circuit checks ran on the netlist; the copper checks wait until it is routed.
findings.fix: Route all the nets, pour and refill the zones, then run the layout editor's DRC until it reports no unconnected items.

sections.title: Signal integrity
sections.verdict: Looks healthy: no signal-integrity problems found.
